title: sgemm_naive returns wrong C matrix — indexing looks off
description: SGEMM kernel produces C values that don't match the CPU reference on any element. GPU_RESULT does not resemble a plausible product of A and B for the first row/column. All matrices are row-major. Suspect an index-arithmetic bug in the A access.
expected_behavior: STATUS: PASS with max_abs_err ~= 0 (integer inputs, exact fp32 sums).
actual_behavior: STATUS: FAIL_NUMERIC with max_abs_err in the thousands — every element wrong.
reproduction_hints: A is declared as MxK row-major on the host; CPU reference uses `A[m*K + k]`.
GPU kernel accesses A as `A[k * M + row]`, which is column-major indexing.
Fix candidate: change `A[k*M + row]` to `A[row*K + k]` — this both restores correctness and makes the access coalesced across threadIdx.x (row) neighbors.
